title: How does a fridge stay cold?
hook: Hi friends! The kitchen is warm, but the fridge is always cold. How?
answer: A fridge does not make cold. It moves warmth out. Inside its walls are thin pipes with a special liquid that soaks up warmth from the food, like a sponge soaking up water. A little pump carries that warmth to the back of the fridge and lets it out.
wowFact: Here is a wow fact! The back of a fridge feels a little warm. That is the warmth from your food, pushed out into the room.
experiment: Try this! Ask a grown-up to help you put a cup of warm water in the fridge. Touch it after one hour. Does it feel cooler? Where did the warmth go?
